subject: pharmacology
title: SSRIs and Venlafaxine: Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Escitalopram, Paroxetine

steps.tx: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors block the serotonin transporter (SERT), raising synaptic serotonin within hours while antidepressant benefit accrues over two to six weeks as autoreceptors desensitise and downstream plasticity adapts, the lag patients must be counselled into surviving. **Fluoxetine**, sertraline, escitalopram and paroxetine share the mechanism and differ in half life, interactions and discontinuation manners, which is where prescribing individuality lives in this class.
steps.say: Transporters block today, mood lifts in weeks; choose the SSRI by its half life and interaction manners.

vis.alt: SSRI and lithium action mechanisms diagram at the synapse
vis.caption: Serotonin transporter blockade at the synapse, the shared opening move of every SSRI in this lesson.

steps.tx: **Fluoxetine** is the long distance runner: parent half life of days and norfluoxetine metabolite of one to two weeks, forgiving missed doses, self tapering on cessation, and haunting CYP2D6 substrates (and tamoxifen activation, and MAO inhibitor washouts of five weeks) long after the last capsule. That tail made it the original weekly formulation candidate and the switch destination when discontinuation symptoms plague shorter agents.
steps.say: Fluoxetine never really leaves quickly: forgiving for adherence, unforgiving for interactions and washouts.

left.title: Fluoxetine conveniences
points: Active metabolite half life 1 to 2 weeks
Missed doses barely register
Discontinuation symptoms rare, self tapering
Useful switch target for discontinuation prone patients

right.title: Fluoxetine complications
points: Potent CYP2D6 inhibition for weeks after stopping
Five week washout before MAO inhibitors
Tamoxifen activation blocked via CYP2D6
Activating early: anxiety and insomnia in some

steps.tx: **Sertraline** balances a middle half life, modest interactions and the class's best cardiac safety dossier after myocardial infarction, becoming the default where hearts and polypharmacy argue, with dose dependent diarrhoea as its signature toll. **Escitalopram**, the S enantiomer of citalopram, offers clean pharmacology with dose dependent QT prolongation capped by age; citalopram's QT ceiling (40 mg, 20 mg over 65 years) is the stricter parent rule examiners quote.
steps.say: Sertraline for hearts and drug lists, escitalopram for cleanliness, QT ceilings respected in the family.

left.title: Sertraline
points: Post myocardial infarction safety evidence
Fewer CYP interactions than fluoxetine or paroxetine
Diarrhoea dose related and characteristic
Broad anxiety disorder licences

right.title: Escitalopram and citalopram
points: Escitalopram: S enantiomer, well tolerated
Dose dependent QT prolongation both agents
Citalopram capped at 40 mg, 20 mg over age 65
Hepatic impairment lowers ceilings further

steps.tx: **Paroxetine** is the class's difficult relation: shortest half life with no active metabolite (discontinuation symptoms fiercest), strongest CYP2D6 inhibition beside fluoxetine, anticholinergic and sedative ballast, weight gain, and the clearest teratogenic signal (first trimester cardiac malformations) that moved it down pregnancy preference lists. It remains effective, particularly for anxiety spectra, but new starts choose it last in most modern formularies for these cumulative reasons.
steps.say: Paroxetine works and misbehaves on every axis that matters; start it last, stop it slowest.

nodes.label: Shortest half life, no active metabolite
Missed doses trigger discontinuation symptoms within days
Taper over weeks, liquid formulations help

steps.tx: **Shared SSRI adverse grammar**: early nausea, headache and activation or jitteriness in week one (start low in panic), sexual dysfunction in a third to a half (the leading reason for silent discontinuation, asked about directly), hyponatraemia via SIADH in the elderly, increased bleeding with NSAIDs and anticoagulants because platelets cannot load serotonin, and discontinuation syndromes graded by half life. Most early effects fade by week two, which the first review exists to testify.
steps.say: Ask about sex, sodium and bruising by name; week one nausea usually leaves before the mood arrives.

left.title: Early and transient
points: Nausea, headache, jitteriness in week one
Usually settle by the second week
Start low in panic disorder
Sleep disturbance either direction

right.title: Persistent and structural
points: Sexual dysfunction until dose or agent changes
Hyponatraemia risk in elderly and diuretic users
Bleeding risk stacked with NSAIDs and anticoagulants
Discontinuation symptoms on abrupt stopping

steps.tx: Shared SSRI harms include a **discontinuation syndrome** graded by half life, worse after a short acting drug than a long acting one. The first week brings nausea, headache and jitteriness, so panic is started low. Sexual dysfunction in a third to a half of patients is the main silent reason for stopping and must be asked about. Older adults develop hyponatraemia through SIADH, and bleeding rises with NSAIDs or anticoagulants because platelets cannot store serotonin. Early effects usually fade by week two.
steps.say: Discontinuation symptoms after an SSRI are worse when the half life is short. The first week also brings nausea, headache and jitteriness, so treatment of panic starts low. Sexual dysfunction in a large minority is a common unspoken reason for stopping and has to be asked about. Elderly patients risk low sodium, and bleeding rises if NSAIDs or anticoagulants are added. Early nausea usually settles by week two.

vis.alt: A scale ranks SSRI discontinuation symptoms as most severe for paroxetine and least severe for fluoxetine, in order of half life.
vis.caption: Discontinuation distress is ranked by SSRI half life, greatest after paroxetine and least after fluoxetine. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Venlafaxine** graduates from SSRI to SNRI (serotonin noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor) as dose climbs beyond 150 mg, recruiting noradrenergic analgesia and activation, with dose dependent hypertension demanding pressure monitoring, the class's most abrupt discontinuation syndrome (its half life is five hours), and sweating, tremor and sexual effects in train. Desvenlafaxine is its active metabolite sold directly, metabolism simplified. In overdose venlafaxine seizes and prolongs QT more readily than SSRIs, a toxicology distinction worth its step.
steps.say: Venlafaxine earns its second letter above 150 mg, and charges hypertension and a brutal discontinuation for it.

left.title: Venlafaxine profile
points: Serotonin only at low dose, SNRI beyond 150 mg
Dose dependent blood pressure elevation
Worst in class discontinuation syndrome
Extended release smooths peaks, not withdrawal

right.title: Prescribing discipline
points: Blood pressure at baseline and after increases
Taper in small decrements over weeks
Overdose: seizures and QT effects exceed SSRIs
Avoid abrupt cessation perioperatively without planning

steps.tx: **Switching and stopping** obey washout physics: cross tapering is safe among most SSRIs and SNRIs, but MAO inhibitors demand two weeks after most (five after fluoxetine) before starting and two weeks after stopping before an SSRI begins, because serotonin syndrome (next lessons) is the collision being avoided. Discontinuation symptoms (dizziness, electric shock sensations, irritability, flu like malaise) are physiology, not addiction, and reinstatement relieves them within a day, proving the taper merely needs lengthening.
steps.say: Washouts guard against serotonin syndrome; discontinuation zaps mean slow the taper, not restart forever.

nodes.label: Switch planned: check half lives and MAO involvement
Washout 2 weeks, 5 after fluoxetine, before MAOI
Cross taper permitted among SSRIs and SNRIs carefully
Final taper slowed over weeks to months

steps.tx: **Pregnancy and adolescence** frame the class's public controversies: untreated depression carries its own obstetric risks, SSRIs as a class show small absolute increases in persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn late in pregnancy, paroxetine carries the cardiac signal above, and neonatal adaptation syndrome (jitteriness, feeding difficulty) follows late exposure transiently. Adolescent prescribing carries suicidality warnings from trial meta analyses, mandating close early follow up whichever agent, fluoxetine best evidenced, is chosen.
steps.say: Weigh untreated illness beside small absolute drug risks, and follow adolescents weekly at the start.

left.title: Pregnancy arithmetic
points: Untreated depression: relapse and obstetric risks
Paroxetine first trimester cardiac signal
Late exposure: neonatal adaptation, transient
Small persistent pulmonary hypertension absolute increase

right.title: Adolescent safeguards
points: Fluoxetine best evidenced in youth depression
Suicidality warning class wide in labelling
Weekly early follow up and family briefing
Combined psychological therapy where available
